title: reliability-liaison-playbook-and-30-60-90-experiments
content:
Purpose and context

This is a working playbook for SRE "liaisons" embedded with product and serving teams to run short, measurable experiments that translate reliability goals into concrete SLOs and operational controls. The intent: make SLO/experiment work low-friction across teams so stability improvements land quickly and are observable.

High-level goals
- Establish a repeatable 30/60/90 day experiment cadence that any feature team can run with SRE support.
- Produce three validated SLOs per major service area (api-gateway, inference-runtime, cache-layer) by end of quarter.
- Reduce customer-facing P95 latency variance by 20% on targeted endpoints within 90 days.
- Capture runbook and handoff artifacts during experiments so oncall can operate post-rollout.

Scope and constraints
- Focus services: api-gateway (hosted-api), serving-runtime (inference), kv-cache (redis/proxy) for Q1 experiments.
- Excludes: dedicated capacity billing changes, long-term infra refactors (these are blockers and will be surfaced).
- Experiment teams expected to deliver telemetry and a lightweight eval harness (latency and correctness checks).

Who does what (liaison model)
- SRE Liaison (primary): Ava Chen — coordinates experiments, shepherds SLO drafts, runs postmortem/retro.
- Product Liaison: Marcus Patel — defines feature/operator stakes and customer impact thresholds.
- Runtime SME: Sofia Martinez — validates feasible measurement signal and assists with kv-cache instrumentation.
- Platform Eng Contact: Ethan Moore — capacity and rollout support for canary/fallback policies.
- Success/TPM: Priya Rao — stakeholder comms, ensures cross-team meetings and deliverable deadlines.

Experiment cadence (30/60/90 template)
- Day 0 (kickoff): Align on hypothesis, success criteria, measurement signal, and initial draft SLO. Create JIRA ticket and link to this doc.
- Day 1-14 (30-day sprint): Implement instrumentation, baseline measurement, short-lived safety canary (1% traffic), and initial runbook sketch. Daily syncs with SRE liaison.
- Day 15-30: Analyze canary results, tweak alert thresholds, expand canary to 10% if OK. Produce interim report.
- Day 31-60 (60-day expansion): If metrics stable, define final SLO target, run fault-injection experiment (rate-limited), document fallback behaviors, and onboard oncall.
- Day 61-90 (90-day validation): Full rollout to production cohort, finalize runbook, establish alert/issue triage flows, and sign SLO into steady-state ownership. Retro and action log.

Concrete example experiment (api-gateway request-latency SLO)
- Hypothesis: Request p95 latency spikes are caused by occasional large model loads and can be mitigated via routing controls and adaptive KV caching.
- Measurement signal: p95 request latency for /v1/generate (30s rolling window), error rate (4xx/5xx), and request token count.
- Initial SLO proposal: 99% of requests under 300ms p95 over 7-day window, error budget 0.5%/30d. (draft — subject to product stake validation).
- Canary: route 1% traffic to route-with-cache-ttl-2s and compare.
- Success criteria: 10% reduction in p95 without >0.1% increase in error rate.

Experiment matrix (quick notes)
- Axis: mitigation (routing, batching, cache), injection (none, small spike, rolling degradation), metric (p50/p95/p99, errors, cpu/mem).
- Prioritization: start with highest customer impact endpoints, low-risk interventions (observability + routing) before infra changes.

Runbook fragments (to be expanded per experiment)
- Pre-rollout checklist: telemetry dashboards created, alert thresholds set to page-test channel, rollback steps documented, capacity reserve validated.
- During-canary steps: check canary dashboard every 15m for first 2h, run smoke correctness test suite on canary traffic, monitor CPU/GPU utilization on inference nodes.
- Rollback: revert routing rule, drain canary nodes via /admin/drain, re-run baseline measurement to confirm normalization.

SLO drafting guide (liaison cheat-sheet)
- Choose signal closest to customer experience (latency for interactive endpoints, success rate for synchronous tasks).
- Window selection: 7d for fast experiments, 30d for production SLOs.
- Error budget math: express in simple terms (e.g., 0.5% over 30d ~ 21.6 minutes). Use this for automated guardrails.
- Dependencies: enumerate infra, data plane, and ops teams who must approve telemetry.

Communications and stakeholder rituals
- Weekly experiment sync (30 min) — standing meeting with product, runtime, platform, SRE liaison.
- Twice-weekly oncall touchpoint during risky rollouts.
- Experiment triage Slack channel naming convention: #sre-liaison-<team>-<experiment>.
- One-pager at the end of each 30/60/90 cycle posted to Confluence (link back in JIRA).

Metrics and dashboards to create
- Canary vs baseline comparison panels: p50/p95/p99, request rate, error rate, token distribution, CPU/GPU utilization.
- SLO burn-rate per service with alerting on burn-rate >2x.
- Observability health: percent of requests with full KV cache hit vs miss.

Risks and mitigations
- Risk: Experiment causes regression in correctness. Mitigation: include end-to-end correctness smoke and shrink canary immediately.
- Risk: Measurement signal polluted by client retries. Mitigation: dedupe retry traffic in telemetry or exclude via header.
- Risk: Rollouts collide with other platform changes. Mitigation: calendar gating (check platform freeze windows) and pre-announce via weekly sync.

Handoff and steady-state ownership
- At validation (end of 90 days) the owning feature team must: adopt SLO dashboard, own alert paging configuration, and commit to weekly SLO review for first 30 days.
- SRE provides a short-term runbook for first-oncall and a long-form runbook for knowledge base.

Notes to self / open questions
- What is acceptable customer impact for experiments on paid tier vs free tier? (action: follow up with product pricing team).
- Need a lightweight eval harness template for runtime teams — add to repo (TODO assigned to Sofia).
- Should we standardize SLO naming and tagging for automated reports? yes — propose tag format: service.environment.slo.<metric>.

Next actions (owner: Ava)
- Create JIRA epic that captures the 30/60/90 experiment plan and link to this doc (by EOD 2026-02-12).
- Prototype a canary dashboard template and push as a Grafana folder (target 2026-02-20).
- Schedule initial liaison sync with api-gateway owners and platform (target 2026-02-15).

Appendix: quick templates
- Draft SLO statement: "Service X will serve requests with p95 latency < TARGET over a 30-day rolling window, with an error budget of <Y>% over 30 days."
- Minimal runbook header: owner, escalation path, runbook steps, rollback commands, links to dashboards.

Document history
- 2026-02-10: initial draft (Ava Chen)
- 2026-02-18: added experiment cadence and example (Sofia Martinez)
- 2026-03-01: updated owners and next actions after sync (Marcus Patel)

-- end working draft --
